chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu al-Abbas, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who leads a woman in prayer in his house, and he said, 'Yes, she stands behind him.'
ai.seo_question: Where should a woman stand when praying behind a man in a house?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the domestic application of *imamah*, confirming that a woman standing behind her husband is legally valid even outside the mosque. This ruling underscores the flexibility of Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between the communal mosque hierarchy and the private household structure where the husband’s leadership is affirmed.
